# Fractional convex-hull packing: exact LP facts and proved bounds

Let P be a finite subset of R^n, let w_v>=0 have total M>0, and let z be any candidate point. Define f_w(z) as the maximum of sum_A lambda_A over nonempty subsets A of P satisfying z in conv(A), with lambda_A>=0 and

sum_{A containing v} lambda_A<=w_v for every v in P.

This is the proposed fractional Tverberg packing value. It is not automatically equal to Tukey depth.

## 1. Finite LP and dual

It suffices to use inclusion-minimal qualifying subsets A. Each has at most n+1 points by Caratheodory. Replacing any larger group by a contained qualifying subset preserves its packing value and only decreases source usage.

The primal feasible region is compact: every group is nonempty, so sum_A lambda_A<=sum_v w_v=M. It is nonempty because the zero packing is feasible. Thus an optimum exists. Finite linear-programming duality gives

f_w(z)=min sum_v w_v t_v,

subject to t_v>=0 and sum_{v in A}t_v>=1 for every minimal qualifying A. If there are no qualifying groups, the optimum is zero.

One can always take 0<=t_v<=1. Clipping a coordinate above one down to one preserves every constraint containing it, since that coordinate alone still supplies one; constraints not containing it are unchanged. Thus the dual minimum is over a fixed compact polytope independent of w.

Consequently f_w(z) is nondecreasing, positively homogeneous, concave, and piecewise linear in w, and

|f_w(z)-f_{w'}(z)|<=sum_v |w_v-w'_v|.

Superadditivity also follows directly by adding two feasible packings at the same center:

f_{w+w'}(z)>=f_w(z)+f_{w'}(z).

For a fixed finite candidate set, its maximum packing value is continuous in the weights. Therefore a conjectural universal assertion for strictly positive weights on a fixed finite lattice-convex set extends to nonnegative weights by adding epsilon to every zero weight and taking epsilon to zero. A selected center can be kept constant along a subsequence because the candidate set is finite.

## 2. Relation to halfspace depth

Let delta_w(z) be unnormalized closed-halfspace depth for the point measure with masses w_v. Then

f_w(z)<=delta_w(z).

Indeed every qualifying group A meets every closed halfspace H containing z; otherwise conv(A) would lie in the open complementary halfspace. Thus

sum_A lambda_A<=sum_A lambda_A |A intersect H|<=sum_{v in H}w_v.

Taking the appropriate maximum and infimum proves the inequality.

There is also a proved lower bound, for n>=1:

f_w(z)>=[delta_w(z)+(n-1)w_z]/n,

where w_z=0 if z is not a source point.

Proof. Use an optimal packing with minimal groups. The singleton {z}, when available, has packing value w_z; no other minimal group contains z. Let r_v be the unused capacity at each source point. The convex hull of the points with r_v>0 cannot contain z, since a sufficiently small additional qualifying group would then improve the packing. If unused points exist, strictly separate their compact convex hull from z by a halfspace through z; perturb the normal slightly so no other source point is on its boundary. If no unused points exist, choose any such generic halfspace through z.

Every source point in this halfspace is saturated. Every nonsingleton minimal group has z in the relative interior of its convex hull. It therefore has at least one vertex on each side of this generic hyperplane, and at most n vertices in the selected halfspace. Hence that halfspace's mass is at most

w_z+n(f_w(z)-w_z)=n f_w(z)-(n-1)w_z.

Its mass is at least delta_w(z), proving the bound. This is an actual packing bound; it does not silently identify packing with Tukey depth.

For finite lattice-convex P subset Z^n, weighted Doignon centerpoints therefore imply the unconditional scale

max_{z in P} f_w(z)>=M/[n 2^n], n>=1.

This is weaker than the proposed M/2^n for n>=2. For uniform unit weights, the same proof gives at the selected lattice center

f(z)>=[ceil(|P|/2^n)+n-1]/n.

## 3. Complete one-dimensional result

In one dimension, write L_z and R_z for the weights strictly to the left and right of z. Then

f_w(z)=w_z+min(L_z,R_z)=delta_w(z).

Use the singleton with value w_z, and pair arbitrary left-side and right-side sources by fractional transport of total min(L_z,R_z). Every such pair contains z in its segment. Conversely, every qualifying group not using z contains a source on each side, so its total packing value is at most the smaller side mass. A weighted median source point consequently has f_w(z)>=M/2. This proves the proposed bound for n=1. For n=0 there is only one candidate point and f=M.

## 4. A rigorous reduction for a hypothetical minimal counterexample

Assume a counterexample to max_z f_w(z)>=M/2^n exists, allowing nonnegative weights as justified above. Choose one minimizing the number of positive-weight sources. The convex hull of those sources must have more than2^n vertices.

Otherwise let its r<=2^n vertices have minimum weight delta>0, and remove capacity delta from every one of them. The remaining measure has fewer positive-weight sources. If its mass M' is positive, minimality gives a lattice center z in its convex hull with packing value at least M'/2^n; if M'=0, choose any lattice point in the original hull. In either case z lies in the convex hull of the removed vertices. Those removed capacities therefore support an additional group of value delta at the same z. The combined value is at least

delta+(M-r delta)/2^n>=M/2^n,

a contradiction. Caratheodory can reduce the added vertex group if desired, but using the full vertex set is already a valid packing group.

Thus any minimal obstruction has more than2^n actual hull vertices with positive weight, and hence a same-parity pair of distinct such vertices. This reduction does not itself show how to merge that pair without losing the target.

## 5. An exact sufficient peeling certificate

Repeatedly subtract the smallest positive hull-vertex weight from every vertex of the current positive-support hull, recording the subtracted amount delta_j and the number r_j of such vertices, until all weights vanish. If a chosen lattice point z belongs to every recorded hull, the recorded vertex groups pack at z with total value sum_j delta_j. Such a z can be chosen in the last nonempty hull, which is nested inside all earlier hulls. Since M=sum_j r_j delta_j, this proves the desired bound whenever

sum_j r_j delta_j<=2^n sum_j delta_j.

In particular it works if every encountered hull has at most2^n vertices. No claim that this condition always holds is made.
